brief:
- Bruising: possible warfarin + NSAID bleeding. Warfarin 5 mg daily [Sunrise Medical Center] plus ibuprofen 400 mg three times daily since Nov 2 [Harbor City Hospital]. Last INR 2.4 was before the NSAID [Sunrise Medical Center]; consider INR today.
- Rash: penicillin allergy with hives [Sunrise Medical Center], yet Augmentin (amoxicillin-clavulanate) given Nov 2–8 [Harbor City Hospital]. Consider drug reaction.
- Two calcium channel blockers: amlodipine [Sunrise Medical Center] and nifedipine XL [Maple Family Clinic].
- Kidneys: eGFR 62 → 48 [Sunrise Medical Center → Maple Family Clinic] while on metformin and an NSAID.
- Background: atrial fibrillation, hypertension, type 2 diabetes. 6 active meds from 3 prescribers.

answers.a: Most likely contributor in the records: warfarin 5 mg daily [Sunrise Medical Center] combined with ibuprofen 400 mg three times daily, started Nov 2 [Harbor City Hospital]. NSAIDs add bleeding risk and can raise INR. His last INR, 2.4, was on Sep 20, before the ibuprofen [Sunrise Medical Center]. Consider checking INR and platelets today.

answers.q: Could the rash be a drug reaction?
answers.a: Possibly. He has a documented penicillin allergy with hives and facial swelling, recorded 2019 [Sunrise Medical Center]. The ER prescribed Augmentin (amoxicillin-clavulanate, a penicillin) Nov 2–8, and noted allergies as 'NKDA? pt unsure' [Harbor City Hospital]. The rash began about 5 days ago, during that course.

answers.q: What is he taking for blood pressure?
answers.a: Two drugs of the same class: amlodipine 5 mg daily since 2021 [Sunrise Medical Center] and nifedipine XL 30 mg daily since Aug 22 [Maple Family Clinic]. The clinic note says he did not mention other medications at that visit [Maple Family Clinic].

answers.q: Is his kidney function OK for metformin?
answers.a: eGFR fell from 62 on 2025-12-05 [Sunrise Medical Center] to 48 on 2026-08-22 [Maple Family Clinic]. He takes metformin 500 mg twice daily [Maple Family Clinic] and is now on ibuprofen [Harbor City Hospital]. No result since the ibuprofen started; consider rechecking renal function and reviewing the metformin dose.

Items the records point to, for your judgment: (1) ibuprofen while on warfarin [Harbor City Hospital, Sunrise Medical Center]; INR not checked since. (2) Penicillin allergy vs recent Augmentin [Sunrise Medical Center, Harbor City Hospital]; update allergy lists. (3) Duplicate calcium channel blockers [Sunrise Medical Center, Maple Family Clinic]. (4) Falling eGFR with metformin and an NSAID [Maple Family Clinic].
